title: Quote-to-Cash Exceptions & Billing Latency Remediation Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the operational process, SLAs, and escalation paths for handling quote-to-cash exceptions and billing latency incidents at Redwood Inference. It covers the most common failure modes between Sales/Procurement contracts and Finance billing systems, remediation runbooks, ownership, and post-incident accounting steps to ensure accurate revenue recognition and customer communication.

Scope

- Applies to: enterprise and dedicated-capacity orders, change-of-term amendments (SOW/PO), marketplace reseller transactions, and manual invoicing.
- Excludes: ad-hoc refunds for marketing credits (governed by Marketing Ops) and customer support credits for trial accounts (governed by CS credit policy).

Definitions

- Billing Latency: time elapsed between a billable event (contract activation/usage window end) and the customer receiving an invoice or billing record in billing pipeline.
- Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) Exception: any mismatch or failure in the pipeline from contract signature to cash collection, including pricing mismatch, missing PO, invoice not generated, incorrect GL allocation, or failed payment capture.
- True-up: the periodic reconciliation that adjusts customer billing for actual usage vs committed amounts.

Service-level targets (operational SLAs)

- Invoice generation SLA: 48 business hours from contract activation or billing period end for standard enterprise contracts.
- Contract ingestion SLA: 24 hours from executed contract uploaded to CPQ/Salesforce and marked as 'Billable' for Finance-led pipelines.
- True-up processing SLA: initial notification to customer within 10 business days following billing period close; adjustments applied in next invoice cycle unless manual credit is required.
- Exception triage SLA: initial triage and incident owner assignment within 4 business hours of ticket creation.
- Revenue recognition data availability: GL posting student feed to RevRec pipeline within 72 hours of invoice issuance for standard invoices; 24 hours for high-priority enterprise deals (see priority tiers below).

Priority tiers

1. P0 — Customer-visible outage impacting multiple customers or a single customer >$250k ARR (Immediate on-call page).
2. P1 — Single-customer invoice missing or materially incorrect (> $50k) or legal/contract dispute that blocks billing (workday SLA: 4 hours initial response).
3. P2 — Routine latency or mismatched metadata affecting < $50k and not blocking cash collection (24-hour initial response).

Ownership and roles

- Finance (Billing Ops) — Overall owner of remediation and communication for billing issues; responsible for invoice issuance, credits, and GL mappings.
- SalesOps / Commercial Ops — Owner for contract metadata and CPQ/SFDC ingestion; validates pricing and amendment mapping.
- Legal — Reviews contract language for billing/termination disputes; approves credit and settlement terms for exceptions > $100k.
- Procurement / Sourcing — For vendor-sourced customer POs, validates PO terms/PO-number mapping and escalates vendor disputes.
- Platform Engineering (Billing Platform Team) — Fixes pipeline failures, queue backpressure, connector issues to accounting systems, and implements monitoring/alerts.
- Customer Success — Customer-facing communications and coordination on billing questions and credit timing.

Quick-reference escalation matrix

- Triage owner: Billing Ops (primary) — page on-call if P0/P1.
- Engineering escalation: Billing Platform On-call (Slack: #oncall-billing) for connector failures / queue backpressure.
- Legal escalation: Legal on-call (email legal-oncall@redwood.ai) for disputes or contract interpretation impacting billing.
- Executive notification: for P0 incidents or repeated P1 incidents affecting >3 customers in a 7-day window.

Incident runbook (step-by-step)

1) Create ticket: Finance creates a Q2C-Exception ticket in JIRA project FIN-BILL with label 'q2c-exception' and include: customer name, contract id, SFDC opportunity id, invoice id (if available), amount impact, and priority tier.
2) Immediate triage (within 4 business hours): Billing Ops confirms facts and assigns to owner. If the root cause is pipeline (queue/concurrency/connector), page Billing Platform. If contract metadata is missing, notify SalesOps.
3) Short-term remediation (containment):
   - If invoice not generated: run targeted invoice-generation job for contract id (BillingOps CLI example below).
   - If payment failed: attempt retry per payment gateway policy (2 retries over 72 hours) and notify AR.
   - If pricing mismatch: suspend further billing under the disputed contract; issue temporary pro-forma invoice if requested by customer.
4) Communication:
   - Send an initial acknowledgement to customer within 6 business hours for P0/P1 and 24 hours for P2. Use subject prefix: [Billing Exception] <Customer> — <short summary>.
   - Example acknowledgement template (short):
     "Hello <Customer>, we are investigating a billing issue related to <contract id>. Our Billing Ops lead <name> will follow up within X hours with an ETA for resolution. We apologize for the inconvenience."
5) Resolution and verification:
   - Confirm invoice issued or credit applied, verify GL mapping and revrec feed ingestion.
   - For manual credits: record credit memo id and reason in FIN-BILL ticket and attach approval evidence.
6) Close ticket and postmortem:
   - For P0/P1 incidents, produce a 72-hour incident summary (owner, timeline, root cause, corrective actions) and schedule a 1-week retrospective with Platform/Finance/SalesOps/Legal.

BillingOps CLI sample commands (internal tooling)

- Re-run invoice generation for contract: 
  ./billingctl generate-invoice --contract-id=CON-12345 --run-mode=ad-hoc --notify=true

- Query delayed invoices: (example SQL run by billing-runbook role)
  SELECT contract_id, created_at, status, last_error FROM billing.invoices WHERE status IN ('pending', 'failed') AND created_at < now() - interval '48 hours';

- Trigger revrec feed export: 
  ./revrec export --invoice-id INV-67890 --target=revrec-staging --priority=high

Common root causes and remediation patterns

1. Contract metadata mismatch (common): missing PO number, mismatched billing address, or incorrect CLM-to-CPQ mapping. Remediation: SalesOps updates SFDC, re-ingest contract, then BillingOps re-runs ingestion job.
2. Connector/backpressure failures (platform): queued messages exceed threshold (see monitoring thresholds below). Remediation: scale billing-workers temporarily, clear poison messages, and apply fix to connector.
3. Manual amendments not flagged as billable: Sales marked amendment as admin-only. Remediation: Legal/SalesOps confirm amendment, patch CPQ metadata, and issue corrected invoice.
4. Currency rounding or tax calculation discrepancies: Finance applies a short-term credit to align with tax rules and files a JIRA to update tax engine config.

Monitoring & alert thresholds

- Pending-invoice queue length > 200 for > 15 minutes -> Pager to Billing Platform on-call.
- Invoice generation failure rate > 1% for rolling 1-hour window -> Alert to #monitoring-billing and Billing Ops.
- Contract ingestion backlog > 24 hours -> Alert to SalesOps and Billing Ops.

Post-incident accounting checklist (required before close)

- Confirm invoice(s) issued or credit memo created and attached to ticket.
- Validate GL accounts and revrec mapping. Attach screenshots of GL entries and RevRec feed acceptance log.
- For exceptions with customer credits > $25k, obtain Legal approval (email chain or redwood-legal JIRA) and CFO sign-off.
- Update contract metadata source and pipeline runbook to prevent recurrence (link change to commit or runbook update).

Change controls and permanent fixes

- Any permanent code change to billing platform must include: unit tests, integration test that covers the failing scenario, a canary roll on staging with sample enterprise contract, and a rollback plan.
- Configuration changes (tax rules, connector endpoints) require a post-change verification run and a signed change ticket in FIN-CHANGES.

Appendix A — Sample mapping table (invoice -> revrec)

| Invoice Line Item | Billing Product Code | RevRec Product | GL Account | Notes |
|-------------------|----------------------|----------------|------------|-------|
| Dedicated: GPU 1x | DED-GPU-1           | Dedicated-Compute | 4001      | Use committed price tier mapping |
| Hosted API: tokens | HOST-TOKENS         | API-Revenue    | 4010      | Per-token meter; tiered pricing applied |
| Support: enterprise | ENT-SUPPORT         | Support-Revenue | 4020     | Recognize ratably over SLA term |

Appendix B — Sample legal clause for SOW amendments (suggested wording)

"Any changes to billable scope or pricing must be documented in a signed amendment and flagged as 'Billable' in Salesforce. Redwood Inference reserves the right to withhold invoice generation until billable status is confirmed. Disputed invoices shall be communicated within thirty (30) days of invoice issuance; failure to dispute within that period constitutes acceptance for billing purposes."

Appendix C — Communication templates

- Customer initial acknowledgement (P1):
  Subject: [Billing Exception] <Customer name> — Invoice delay for <contract id>
  Body: Hello <Customer>,

  We are investigating a billing delay for contract <contract id>. Our Billing Ops lead <name> will provide an update within 4 hours and an ETA for resolution. We will not take collection actions until this is resolved.

  Regards,
  Redwood Billing Ops

- Internal status update cadence: every 2 hours for P0 incidents, every business day for P2.

Owner and review cadence

- Document owner: Head of Billing Ops (Finance).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review with SalesOps, Platform Eng, and Legal to update SLAs, thresholds, and templates.
